transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-16 14:00 PDT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Jasmine Park, Leo Martinez, Priya Rao (Redwood); Marcus Lee, Ana Duarte, Samir Patel (Nebula)

Auto-summary (auto): The call focused on repeated cold-start latency at Nebula, which manifests as 5-12s spikes on first requests after scale-to-zero and intermittent KV cache misses after node upgrades. We went through instrumentation gaps and tactical mitigations.

--- Topics covered:
- Where cold starts appear in the pipeline (model load vs runtime init)
- Warmup strategies (prefetching embeddings, priming KV cache)
- Tradeoffs: pre-provisioned capacity vs cost
- Short-term mitigations and observability improvements

--- Action items (see metadata list)

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jasmine: okay good morning everyone, thanks for joining. I think we have about 50 minutes, want to focus on the cold start pain you're seeing in checkout NLU, can you, Marcus, give a quick status?
[00:28] Marcus: yeah thanks. So over the last two weeks we've had these large p99 spikes like on Friday, we saw a 9 second jump for the first inference after a node reboot, subsequent tokens were fine, so it looks like model load/time-to-first-token.
[00:45] Ana: and to add, sometimes when we redeploy the infra, the KV cache doesn't repopulate so early requests also hit full compute path. It's kind of a double whammy.
[01:12] Leo: okay so two things: model binary load/RT init and KV cache priming. Do you have the model sizes and quantization levels?
[01:28] Ana: currently two families: small-retail-1 (2.4B float16) and check-intent-v1 (7.1B int8-quant). We do convert some to int8 but the 7B still does a lot of IO on first load.
[01:50] Samir: right and our autoscaler is set to aggressive downscale at 5m of idle. That saves cost but then when traffic returns it's scale-up then model load costs.
[02:09] Jasmine: classic latency/cost triangle. Quick q: are you running dedicated or hosted?
[02:16] Marcus: dedicated pools in us-west-2; but some ephemeral worker nodes come up in different AZs during maintenance.
[02:28] Leo: got it. So two vectors: make model load faster (warm binaries, lazy layers, optimized IO paths) and reduce user-visible cold windows (warmup daemon, pre-provision short-lived tickets).
[02:48] Ana: curious about warmup daemon approach, does Redwood have a reference?
[02:55] Leo: we do have internal experiments — a lightweight daemon that opens the model, runs a short generation prefix to populate the KV cache and leaves the process runnable without taking heavy GPU alloc. The trick is safe memory reclaim and not increasing GPU residency cost.
[03:18] Marcus: so basically spin up, run one warm request per model, then keep it in a reserved pool? How does it interact with your autoscaler?
[03:28] Leo: two ways: either pre-provision a tiny reserved pool (1-2 instances) or have burst nodes with warmup hook — when a node boots it runs the daemon before joining LB. Autoscaler needs a pre-ready signal.
[03:44] Samir: does that affect SLOs for concurrent loads? If we have warmups happening they shouldn't disrupt live capacity.
[03:55] Leo: right, warmup should be async and low priority; we can throttle it. Also you can use GPU-shared modes to keep binaries resident with low compute. There are perf tradeoffs though.
[04:15] Ana: you mentioned KV cache priming. How do we capture keys to prime? If we just do a generic prefix it might not load relevant tokens.
[04:25] Leo: good point. We usually take a short set of representative prompts (from recent traffic) and run those during warmup. That primes common attention patterns and tokens. Ideally you ship a small prompt set from telemetry.
[04:42] Marcus: we can export top-100 recent prefixes from our analytics cluster, but privacy scrubbed. Is that enough?
[04:52] Jasmine: yes that's usually plenty. Even a dozen high-frequency prefixes can dramatically reduce first-request latency.
[05:05] Ana: what's the expected reduction?
[05:09] Leo: in our internal tests we saw first-token time drop from ~7-10s to ~1.2-2s depending on model and IO backplane. But results vary.
[05:28] Samir: wow that's a lot. Are there any correctness risks? Like model state leaking between requests?
[05:35] Leo: you have to ensure warmup runs with a dedicated context and clears ephemeral state; warmup should only prime KV caches and not persist session-level state. We'll need to validate in staging.
[05:49] Marcus: instrumentation — how do we tell if a request is cold vs warm in traces? We don't have a cold-start flag right now.
[05:58] Priya: quick note, we should add a span attribute e.g., cold.start=true and expose time-to-first-token metric. We're lacking that currently.
[06:12] Ana: where would Redwood add that? At the SDK or infra layer?
[06:18] Leo: infra layer is easiest — the runtime can emit a metric on first token served after model load. We'll propose an event tag and an example OpenTelemetry schema.
[06:31] Marcus: great. What about short-term tactics if we can't roll a daemon soon?
[06:38] Jasmine: some low-effort mitigations: staggered restarts to avoid mass cold windows, increase downscale threshold from 5m to 10m for critical routes, or keep a tiny dedicated hot pool for peak hours.
[06:52] Samir: we could also set a slightly higher min replicas for checkout endpoints only. That would cost more but reduce user regressions.
[07:02] Ana: is there an automated way to detect when warmup is needed vs when traffic is truly gone?
[07:09] Leo: you can use an exponential backoff with hint from request ramp patterns — if a route sees bursts above a threshold you trigger pre-warm. But it's heuristic.
[07:24] Marcus: curious about memory/IO when keeping binaries resident. How much extra does a warm instance take?
[07:31] Leo: depends on model; small-retail-1 about 6GB GPU mem for runtime plus 2-3GB for caches; 7B might be up to 12GB. We can use quantized versions to reduce residency.
[07:48] Ana: our nodes are A10G-like capacities; memory is constrained so we can't hold many warmed 7B at once.
[07:56] Leo: then hybrid approach — keep warm small models and use warmup for big models on demand with pre-warm tickets. Also consider incremental layer loading if model framework supports it.
[08:14] Priya: note for action items: we'll attach recommended quant profiles and a sample warmup daemon code.
[08:23] Jasmine: logistic q: do you want Redwood to run the benchmark against your staging or do you want the script to run it yourselves?
[08:31] Marcus: preferred Redwood run it once to baseline, then we run with our infra changes.
[08:38] Leo: cool, we'll need staging access and sample prompts. Also SSH/console for node boot logs would help.
[08:48] Ana: is there any dependency on KMS or secrets? We use a private key to pull model artifact from our artifact store.
[08:56] Leo: we can work with a service account token scoped to read artifacts in staging; no KMS changes needed unless you want encrypted caches.
[09:05] Samir: timeline? If we get the benchmark this week can we have warmup prototype in two weeks?
[09:12] Leo: yes prototype in ~2 weeks, benchmarks in a few days. We'll aim for daemon PR by Apr 30.
[09:20] Marcus: ok good. Let's talk instrumentation gaps — we don't have first-token histograms per route.
[09:28] Priya: Redwood will share a dashboard template (Grafana) and queries for the first-token metric. That should help track regressions.
[09:36] Ana: also curious about TTL for KV caches, we currently evict at 30m, which might be too short for low-frequency routes.
[09:45] Leo: you can make TTLs route-specific. For checkout route longer TTL makes sense; but stale caches can be a memory hog. Tradeoffs.
[09:57] Marcus: any quick wins on cache strategy?
[10:02] Leo: reduce eviction pressure by prioritizing hot keys, set soft limit eviction and async prefetch on read-miss.
[10:12] Ana: ok. Also we noticed warmup increased ephemeral IO on artifact store — some bursts caused artifactstore rate limits.
[10:22] Leo: warmup should use a cached artifact registry per region or prefetched blobs on nodes. We can add backoff to prevent thundering herd.
[10:35] Jasmine: circling back, could you summarize the recommended immediate config changes?
[10:41] Leo: increase downscale threshold from 5m to 10m for checkout routes, enable one reserved hot replica during peak hours, export top-100 prefixes and provide to us, enable first-token metric.
[10:56] Marcus: agreed. We'll take downscale and reserved replica change in staging tomorrow.
[11:03] Ana: I'll get prefixes by Tue.
[11:08] Samir: I'll extract pod restart/event logs and share.
[11:14] Priya: Redwood will upload the benchmark script and dashboard templates by Apr 23.
[11:20] (brief pause)
[11:30] Leo: quick technical note: when we did warmup in our tests, we saw a small increase in baseline GPU residency cost (about 3-5%) but huge p99 reduction. Need acceptance from finance on that tradeoff.
[11:47] Marcus: we can model that if you provide the numbers.
[11:52] Jasmine: ok final recap and next steps — we listed them in the meta but to recap: Redwood runs benchmark, Nebula provides prefixes + logs, engineering runs a short staging test with downscale tweak, and follow-up meeting to review results.
[12:10] Ana: thanks everyone. That was helpful.
[12:15] Jasmine: thanks all, we'll send notes and action items.

End of transcript.
notes: Contains noisy ASR artifacts (some words merged), speaker attributions may be approximate. References to product internals (warmup daemon) are exploratory proofs of concept, not GA features.
